comments.note: mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts: CLAIMABLE_ROLES is a standalone string array defined locally in work-package.ts rather than being derived from the AGENT_ROLES constant in constants.ts. If a new agent role is added to AGENT_ROLES, the developer must manually decide whether to add it to CLAIMABLE_ROLES. Consider adding a CI-time assertion (e.g. in tests) that verifies every non-orchestrating role in AGENT_ROLES is present in CLAIMABLE_ROLES to prevent silent drift.

mcp-server/tests/tools/work-package.test.ts: The 'rejects Planner role' test assigns the WP to 'Planner' so the assignment guard doesn't block it first. This setup is correct and the comment explains the intent. However, no test covers the case where an unknown/non-claimable role tries to claim a WP assigned to a *different* agent — in that scenario the assignment guard fires first, effectively masking the CLAIMABLE_ROLES guard. This is acceptable behaviour but worth documenting in the test suite.

comments.note: mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts (line 388): CLAIMABLE_ROLES is a standalone string array rather than being derived from AGENT_ROLES in constants.ts. The constants.ts comment states 'All other files that reference agent roles should import from here rather than defining local constants.' While a direct filter isn't possible (AGENT_ROLES lacks the Agent aliases and the exclusion rules differ), a computed approach — e.g. AGENT_ROLES.filter(r => !ORCHESTRATING_ROLES.includes(r)) plus the alias suffix set — would make the exclusion logic explicit and reduce drift risk. Medium priority because silent drift is possible when a new role is added to AGENT_ROLES.

mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts (line 447): The CLAIMABLE_ROLES guard (step 2c) fires after the assignment guard (step 2) and override-auth guard (step 2b). Consequence: a Planner claiming a WP assigned to Developer receives the assignment error, not the role error. This is intentional and documented in tests — but the guard could be moved to step 1b (immediately after the READY check) so role validation is always surfaced regardless of assignment state. Low priority since the QA team has already documented the masking behavior.

mcp-server/src/tools/work-package.ts (line 448): The actionable error hint 'Valid roles: Developer, QA, Reviewer, Documentation, Project Manager.' does not enumerate the Agent-alias variants (e.g., 'Documentation Agent'). Users whose agent name is an alias variant will not trigger the error (aliases are in CLAIMABLE_ROLES), but the hint could be expanded or dynamically generated from CLAIMABLE_ROLES to avoid confusion when reading logs.
